relationship: Changing the seed environment changes differential reproduction of existing inherited beak variation, so trait frequencies change across generations rather than individual birds changing their beaks.

learnerLoop.action: Predict a population change, reshape seed availability, and run selection and inheritance.
learnerLoop.modelChange: The environment biases the parent pool; offspring inherit varied traits before replacing the adult population.
learnerLoop.evidence: Adult and likely-parent distributions, generation history, and mean, spread and middle-band frequencies reveal directional, stabilising or disruptive selection.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Compare the outcome with the prediction, then sustain or reverse the pressure to test the explanation.

invariants: Editing the environment changes likely parents without changing existing adult traits.
Selection precedes inheritance and generation replacement; offspring resemble successful parents with variation.
Distribution and numerical evidence describe the same population and distinguish the three selection patterns.
safeAdaptations: Change organism context or guidance while preserving heritable variation and differential reproduction.
Offer additional seed environments and prediction prompts that test changes in frequency over generations.
nonGoals: Do not portray adaptation as individuals deliberately acquiring a needed trait.
Do not extend this population model into a full genetic or ecological simulator.

goal.description: Directional, stabilising or disruptive population goal.
goal.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

model.description: Seed environment, inherited adult variation and adult/likely-parent histogram aligned by trait.
model.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

decision.description: Prediction and current selection/inheritance/next-generation action beside the plots.
decision.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

evidence.description: Mean/spread/middle-frequency comparison, causal mechanism and generation history.
evidence.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

progress.description: Three investigation checkpoints; previously unlocked investigations remain revisitable.
progress.visibility: Present in the current investigation; child controls follow the mode and state.

environment.domain: Trait axis 4–16 mm; width constrained to 0.55–3 mm.
environment.source: Learner changes one or two food sources.
environment.output: Changes food access and likely reproductive contribution.

trait-frequency.description: Distribution of inherited beak depth in 72 adults.
trait-frequency.source: Adults retain their values; selected parents produce similar offspring with variation.
trait-frequency.output: Next-generation mean, spread and middle/tail frequencies.

prediction.description: Expected direction or shape of population change.
prediction.domain: Mean increase, narrower distribution, or split distribution.

modes.guided: Three successive selection patterns; first generation explicitly separates selection and inheritance. No Working toggle.
modes.free: One/two sources and repeated generations; returning restores guided state.

dependencies: Predict and change the food environment enough to produce a useful parent preview.
Selection precedes offspring production; offspring must replace adults before frequencies change.
Completion requires several generations and the relevant measured distribution change.
implementation.completion: Directional: ≥3 generations and mean increase ≥1.65 mm; stabilising uses generation/spread criterion; disruptive: ≥4 generations, enlarged spread, reduced middle and both tails retained.
limitations: Population size fixed; simplified heritable trait model. No claim that adult birds change their beaks, and no genetic-drift or Hardy–Weinberg model.
